What is Intermediate? Two-year course after 10th (1st year = 11th, 2nd year = 12th). Conducted by TGBIE – Telangana Board of Intermediate Education (earlier TSBIE). Annual public exams in both years (usually Feb–March); results in April. Available in Government Junior Colleges (free), Aided, Private, TG Model Schools, Residential (TSWREIS, TTWREIS, MJPTBCWREIS, TMREIS, KGBV). Admission Eligibility: SSC / 10th pass (any board) – CBSE/ICSE students also eligible. Admission via TGBIE online admission schedule (usually May–June) or directly at college. Residential colleges admit through entrance tests (e.g. TG RJC CET / Gurukul CET). All Streams (Groups) MPC Maths, Physics, Chemistry Engineering, B.Arch, B.Sc, NDA, Defence BiPC Botany, Zoology, Physics, Chemistry MBBS, BDS, Pharmacy, Agriculture, Nursing MEC Maths, Economics, Commerce CA, CMA, CS, B.Com, BBA, Finance CEC Civics, Economics, Commerce B.Com, CA, Banking, BBA HEC History, Economics, Civics BA, Law, Civil Services, Teaching MBiPC* Maths + BiPC (bridge course) Keep both Engineering & Medical options Vocational Job-oriented trades Early employment, Diploma lateral Language Subjects (all groups) Part I: English – 100 marks per year. Part II: Second language – Telugu / Hindi / Sanskrit / Urdu / Arabic / French etc. – 100 marks per year. Ethics & Human Values, Environmental Education (qualifying, not added to total). Pass Percentage Rules Pass mark: 35% in each subject (theory), e.g. 26/75, 21/60, 35/100. Practicals (MPC/B

Who should take MPC Students strong in Maths & science who want Engineering, Architecture, Defence (NDA), pure sciences or data/computer careers. Subjects & Marks (TGBIE) English 100 100 Second Language 100 100 Mathematics IA (Algebra, Vectors, Trigonometry) 75 - Mathematics IB (Coordinate Geometry, Calculus) 75 - Mathematics IIA (Complex Numbers, Probability, Binomial) - 75 Mathematics IIB (Circles, Conics, Integration, DE) - 75 Physics 60 60 + 30 practical Chemistry 60 60 + 30 practical Total 470 530 (Grand total 1000) Pass Percentage Pass mark: 35% in each subject (theory), e.g. 26/75, 21/60, 35/100. Practicals (MPC/BiPC science subjects): 30 marks each in 2nd year; pass needs 35% of practical marks. No overall aggregate needed to pass, but each subject must be cleared separately. Divisions: 75%+ Distinction, 60%+ First Class, 50–59% Second Class, 35–49% Pass. Failed subjects can be cleared in the Advanced Supplementary Exams (May/June) of the same year. Improvement exam: students who passed can rewrite 1st-year papers to improve marks. TGBIE is introducing reforms (internal assessment, revised syllabus). Check tgbie.cgg.gov.in for the latest scheme. Entrance exams you can prepare for during MPC TG EAPCET (Engineering stream) – state engineering seats. JEE Main → NITs, IIITs, GFTIs; JEE Advanced → IITs. BITSAT, VITEEE, SRMJEEE and other private university tests. NDA (UPSC) – can apply in 12th; Indian Navy 10+2 B.Tech entry; Agniveer Vayu. NATA / JEE Main Paper-2 for B.Arch

TG EAPCET (Engineering) Conducted by JNTU Hyderabad on behalf of TGCHE (usually April–May). 160 MCQs, 160 marks, 3 hours: Maths 80, Physics 40, Chemistry 40. No negative marks. Qualifying: 25% (40/160); no minimum for SC/ST for ranking. Inter eligibility for admission: 45% in MPC group subjects (40% reserved categories). Inter marks weightage was removed – rank is based only on EAPCET score. Counselling: TGCHE web options (tgeapcet.nic.in) – convenor seats (fee reimbursement possible for eligible students). JEE Main Conducted by NTA, two sessions (January & April). Paper 1 (B.E/B.Tech): Maths, Physics, Chemistry – 300 marks, negative marking. Admission to NITs (NIT Warangal in Telangana), IIITs (IIIT Hyderabad has own process), GFTIs via JoSAA. Needs 75% in 12th (65% SC/ST) or top-20 percentile for NIT/IIT admission. JEE Advanced Top ~2.5 lakh JEE Main qualifiers can write; admission to IITs (IIT Hyderabad in Telangana). Other exams BITSAT (BITS Hyderabad campus), VITEEE, SRMJEEE, Amrita, MET, KIIT, CUET-UG (some universities). Top engineering colleges in Telangana IIT Hyderabad, NIT Warangal, IIIT Hyderabad, BITS Pilani-Hyderabad. JNTUH College of Engineering (Hyderabad, Sultanpur, Jagtial, Manthani), OU College of Engineering, KU College of Engineering. CBIT, VNR VJIET, Vasavi, MVSR, MGIT, Sreenidhi, CVR, Gokaraju Rangaraju, Mahindra University, etc. Lateral entry Diploma holders join 2nd year B.Tech through TG ECET – see Polytechnic folder.

What is it? 2-year intermediate equal to regular inter, but job-oriented with practical training and on-the-job training (OJT). Offered by TGBIE in Govt Junior Colleges and private vocational colleges. Bridge course allows entry to degree courses; some courses allow lateral entry to Polytechnic 2nd year. Popular vocational courses Engineering & Technology Electrical Technician, Automobile Engineering Technician, Construction Technology, Mechanical Technician, Electronics Technician, Computer Science & Engineering Paramedical Medical Lab Technician (MLT), Multipurpose Health Worker (Female/Male), Ophthalmic Technician, Physiotherapy Technician Business & Commerce Accounting & Taxation, Office Assistantship, Banking & Insurance Agriculture Crop Production, Dairying, Sericulture, Fisheries Home Science & Others Garment Making, Preschool Teacher Training, Tourism & Hospitality, Computer Graphics & Animation Pass percentage 35% in each theory paper; practicals usually require 50%. English + vocational theory + practicals/OJT. Jobs Junior Lineman (electrical), lab assistant, health worker, accounts assistant, private hospitals & industries. Apprenticeship and self-employment.

What is Polytechnic? 3-year diploma in engineering/technology (some 3.5 yrs with 6 months industrial training). Board: TGSBTET – State Board of Technical Education & Training, Telangana. Govt Polytechnics charge very low fees; fee reimbursement for eligible SC/ST/BC/EWS/minority students. Diploma = equivalent to Intermediate for many purposes and allows lateral entry into 2nd year B.Tech. Admission – TG POLYCET Conducted by TGSBTET (usually April–May); eligibility 10th class (appearing students can also apply). Exam: 120 marks, 2 hours – Mathematics 60, Physics 30, Chemistry 30. Agriculture/Veterinary diplomas: Maths/Biology option (PJTSAU, PVNRTVU, SKLTGHU use POLYCET ranks). Qualifying mark 30% (36/120); no minimum for SC/ST. Counselling online: tgpolycet.nic.in – choose branch & college. What is ITI? Skill-based trade courses of 1 or 2 years under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS). Managed in Telangana by the Department of Employment & Training (DET); national standard by DGT (NCVT). Govt ITIs have very low fees; many private ITIs also exist. NEET-UG exam Conducted by NTA, usually on the first Sunday of May. It is a pen-and-paper exam. 180 questions (all compulsory, no optional section), 720 marks, 3 hours. Physics 45, Chemistry 45, Botany 45, Zoology 45. Marking: +4 for a correct answer, −1 for a wrong one, 0 for unattempted. Eligibility: 12th with Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English. What is this course? Many Telangana students study MBBS in Russia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Philippines, Bangladesh, Nepal. t: RMP / PMP 'Village Doctors' – Legal Facts Every Student Must Know
x: Who are RMPs / PMPs? RMP here means 'Rural Medical Practitioner' and PMP means 'Private Medical Practitioner' – people who give treatment in villages without a recognised medical degree. They are NOT Registered Medical Practitioners in law. 'RMP' does not mean 'registered'. What the law says Under the National Medical Commission Act 2019 (Section 34), only a person registered with NMC/State Medical Council (MBBS or higher) may practise modern medicine. Practising without registration: punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year and/or fine up to ₹5 lakh. Prescribing antibiotics/steroids, giving injections, IV drips or running a 'clinic/hospital' without registration is illegal. Telangana State Medical Council and the Drugs Control Administration conduct raids and file cases against unqualified practitioners. Government training (history) Around 2015–2017, Telangana/AP proposed training RMPs/PMPs as 'Community Paramedics' (first-aid level, 6 months). Doctors' associations challenged this in court. It does NOT give a licence to treat patients as a doctor. Our advice Do NOT pay for any 'RMP certificate course' – it gives no legal right to practise. Choose a recognised, legal health career instead (see next file).

t: Legal Ways to Work in Village Health Care
x: Recognised options MBBS 5.5 yrs Doctor – PHC Medical Officer, own clinic BAMS/BHMS/BUMS 5.5 yrs AYUSH doctor – own clinic legally B.Sc Nursing / GNM + CCH 3–4 yrs Community Health Officer at Palle Dawakhana ANM / MPHW (F) 2 yrs Village health worker (mother-child care) MPHW (Male) / Health Assistant Training course Disease control, malaria, sanitation D.Pharm / B.Pharm 2–4 yrs Own medical shop (legal) Paramedical diploma (DMLT etc.) 2 yrs Village diagnostic/lab centre EMT (108 ambulance) Short training Emergency first response ASHA worker Training Village health activist (women, NHM) Why choose a legal path Legal courses give a registration number – you can work in govt hospitals, private hospitals and abroad. Govt jobs (MHSRB, NHM) are open only to registered professionals. You avoid police cases, fines and closure of your clinic. Fast options for village service Inter → ANM/MPHW (2 yrs) → Health worker at sub-centre Inter → D.Pharm (2 yrs) → own medical shop in the village Inter → DMLT (2 yrs) → village diagnostic lab Inter BiPC → B.Sc Nursing (4 yrs) + CCH → Community Health Officer at Palle Dawakhana
